messages.content: The Sunday nonstop is now the return I’m using, so this is Thursday through Sunday after all. Compare the conference hotel with the smaller place nearby before I settle the room.

For June 11-14, the Boston Park Plaza conference offer is $1,146 total for three nights, including estimated taxes and the mandatory destination charge. The smaller hotel is $987 tax-inclusive, a difference of $159. The Park Plaza is the meeting venue, while the smaller hotel is about a nine-minute outdoor walk away or roughly 12-18 minutes by transit once waiting and walking are included.
Remind me how the schedule affects that difference.

Your Thursday flight arrives at 12:50 p.m., leaving ample time to reach either hotel before the 6:30 p.m. dinner at the Park Plaza. Friday begins there at 8:30 a.m. and runs through 5:00 p.m. Saturday also starts at 8:30 and finishes at 4:00. Staying at the Park Plaza removes six round-trip walks and makes both early starts simpler.
What are the cancellation and deposit terms for each? I don’t want the lower total hiding a prepaid rate.

Neither displayed option is fully prepaid. The Park Plaza takes a one-night room-and-tax deposit of $382 at booking; the remainder is due at check-in. It can be canceled without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local hotel time on Monday, June 8. After that, the deposit is forfeited. The smaller hotel takes a $329 first-night deposit and permits free cancellation only through 3:00 p.m. on Sunday, June 7; a later cancellation costs one night.
And for leaving early Sunday? The flight is in the morning.

For the 8:10 a.m. nonstop to Denver, plan to leave the hotel around 5:30 a.m. The Park Plaza front desk and bell service operate around the clock, and it can provide an emailed folio after an express checkout. The smaller hotel’s desk does not open until 7:00 a.m.; it allows key drop and advance settlement Saturday evening, but there would be no staffed checkout or luggage help at departure.
I won’t need luggage storage Sunday, but I would rather have someone available if the bill or car is wrong. Is there any meaningful airport difference?

Not much. By taxi or rideshare at that hour, the Park Plaza estimate is 15-25 minutes and the smaller hotel is 17-27 minutes. Public transit would require an earlier departure and at least one transfer from either property, so a prearranged car or rideshare is the practical plan.
What room choices are behind those totals?

The Park Plaza total is for a standard room with either one king or one queen, assigned subject to availability. The smaller hotel total is for its compact standard queen. The Park Plaza can accept a bed request but does not guarantee it on this rate.
For this solo stay, whichever standard room is available is fine. When my spouse and I share one room, a queen works for us unless I say we need separate beds.
Understood. For Boston I’ll leave the Park Plaza request as any standard room, which avoids tying the selection to a bed type. The quoted total stays $1,146.
Choose the Park Plaza. The $159 is worth avoiding the walks and having a staffed desk Sunday. Put together exactly what should be reserved, but don’t submit it yet.

Reservation record: Boston Park Plaza, one adult, one standard room, check-in Thursday, June 11 and check-out Sunday, June 14, for three nights. Request any available standard bed configuration. Displayed total is $1,146 including estimated taxes and the mandatory destination charge. A $382 deposit is due when booked, with the balance due at check-in. Free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. Boston time Monday, June 8; later cancellation forfeits the deposit. Note the Thursday 6:30 p.m. dinner and Friday and Saturday 8:30 a.m. starts at the hotel. Arrange a car or rideshare for about 5:30 a.m. Sunday, use express checkout, and request an emailed folio. Nothing has been booked; live inventory, the final charge breakdown, exact room assignment terms, and the cancellation deadline must be reconfirmed on the booking screen.
